subject: Clarify: tier sieve, add-on sensitivity, and pilot SKU ask
messages:
From: Alicia Barnes <alicia@medbridge.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedBridge Procurement <procurement@medbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging clarity for pilot – tier vs usage credits

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team found the latency/cost tradeoffs compelling. A couple of procurement questions came up as we scope the pilot:

1) For the pilot (10k monthly active calls, variable token lengths), would you recommend the Compact tier with burst credits or the Throughput tier pinned to a small Dedicated pool? We care most about predictable per-call latency during peak windows.

2) How do add-ons (Streamed responses, Function access, and Extended retention) price against tier seats — is it a flat per-seat uplift or metered? Procurement would like a sensitivity view so we can justify the PO.

3) The RFP appendix asked for an SKU matrix and a sample contract amendment for a short-term seat add. Can you attach both?

Attached: MedBridge-RFP-Appendix.pdf (for context)

Can we get a one-page sensitivity table (price vs expected monthly tokens) and suggested recommendation by Fri so our budget committee can review?

Best,
Alicia Barnes
Head of Integrations
MedBridge

---
MedBridge Procurement: procurement@medbridge.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Barnes <alicia@medbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging clarity for pilot – tier vs usage credits

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear asks and for sending the appendix. Quick answers up front, then details below:

- Recommendation: start pilot on Compact (hosted) + burst credits, add a short Dedicated pilot window only if observed p50/p95 latency under load slips beyond your SLOs. This minimizes up-front commit and gives a clear trigger for Dedicated.
- Add-ons pricing: Streamed responses and Function access are metered (per-call multiplier) while Extended retention is a flat monthly addon per workspace.
- I attached an SKU_matrix_v1.xlsx and a one-page sensitivity table.

Details / rationale:
- Compact + burst lets you get predictable cost while our autoscaling and prefix caching reduce token unit costs during repeated prompts. Dedicated makes sense when sustained QPS requires reserved GPU lanes — for MedBridge size, that threshold is ~120 reqs/min sustained.
- For the sensitivity view I modeled three consumption bands (10k, 35k, 85k calls/mo) and included token mix assumptions (avg input 420 tokens, output 180 tokens).

Next steps / asks:
1) Ben, please review pricing lines and include an explicit short-term amendment example for a +10 seat add-on and for a 60-day Dedicated pilot.
2) Karthik, can you confirm the 120 reqs/min Dedicated threshold and add any operational caveats (KV-cache preload time, warmup for quantized weights)?

Alicia — will schedule a 30-min walkthrough. Available Wed/Thu midday PST.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai
attachment: SKU_matrix_v1.xlsx

Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging clarity for pilot – tier vs usage credits

Adding the concrete numbers Alicia asked for — see the sensitivity snippet below (full table attached in SKU_matrix_v1.xlsx):

- Compact tier (hosted API): base $0.0025 per inference unit (per 1k tokens equivalent), burst credits pool $1,200 for 100k extra tokens/month.
- Throughput (Dedicated) small pool: $6,000/mo reserved; effective unit cost ~30% lower at sustained volumes.
- Streamed responses: +12% per-call multiplier.
- Function access: +$0.03 per invocation for protected tools.
- Extended retention (90 days): $350/mo per workspace.

Example 60-day Dedicated pilot amendment: 50% discount on first 30 days of reserved fee, auto-fallback to hosted if utilization < 40% over pilot window. Draft clause attached.

A few negotiation levers for procurement:
- Commit to a 6-month nominal seat volume and get an extra 6% off list for the period.
- Metered add-ons can be capped with a monthly not-to-exceed line item.

Alicia — if those numbers look reasonable I can put together a short two-column comparison (Cost vs Latency) for your committee.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, GTM Pricing, Redwood Inference
